blocks.content: The first passenger train in India ran on 16 April 1853 between Bombay and Thane over a distance of 34 kilometers.

items: Lord Dalhousie introduced the first passenger railway line in India in 1853.
The world's longest railway platform is at Hubballi Junction (Karnataka), measuring 1,507 meters.
The Railway Budget was merged back with the Union Budget in 2017 based on the Bibek Debroy Committee recommendations.
Kolkata Metro was the first rapid transit system in India, beginning operations in 1984.

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: The first passenger train in India ran between Bombay (Bori Bunder) and Thane on April 16, 1853, covering a distance of 34 km.
Indian Railways was nationalized in 1951 and is currently divided into 19 administrative zones, including Metro Railway Kolkata.
Lord Dalhousie is recognized as the 'Father of Indian Railways' for launching the railway network in British India.
Bholu, an elephant holding a green guard lamp, was introduced in 2002 as the official mascot of Indian Railways.
